meta.document_purpose: Complete technical specification of the MPD Part 107 Readiness app, written for feeding into another AI assistant (e.g. ChatGPT) as context when generating new content (questions, lessons, figures) or requesting code changes. Generated by Claude from the actual live project files, not from memory.
meta.one_line_summary: An internal web app that helps MPD officers study for the FAA's Part 107 UAG (drone pilot) knowledge test, tracks their readiness to schedule the real exam, and gives a coordinator visibility into the whole roster.

tech_stack.styling: Plain CSS with custom design tokens (no Tailwind/component library) -- see design_system section
tech_stack.routing: react-router-dom v6, HashRouter (not BrowserRouter -- chosen so a single static HTML file works without server-side routing config)
tech_stack.database_and_auth: Supabase (Postgres + Supabase Auth), shared with the owner's other personal projects (Operation 200, Bill Planner) -- every table is prefixed part107_ specifically to avoid colliding with those
tech_stack.email: Resend, via a Netlify scheduled function that drains a queue table (not yet fully configured/tested live)
tech_stack.hosting: Netlify, deployed from a GitHub repo (auto-builds on push to main)
tech_stack.build_output: The production build is a SINGLE self-contained index.html file (vite-plugin-singlefile), with every image and script inlined as base64/inline JS -- chosen so it could be deployed via Netlify's drag-and-drop UI without needing git. It has since moved to proper GitHub+Netlify CI, but the single-file build config is still in vite.config.ts.
tech_stack.testing: vitest, covering pure logic only (scoring, sampling, readiness, question-bank integrity) -- no component or end-to-end tests

demo_mode_vs_real_mode.explanation: The app has two operating modes, both using the exact same UI code: if VITE_SUPABASE_URL/VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are not set (or a user isn't signed in), it runs entirely on the browser's localStorage with a single implied 'demo officer' -- no accounts, no server calls, fully offline-usable. If those env vars ARE set and a user signs in, the same pages instead call Netlify Functions and read/write Supabase directly.
demo_mode_vs_real_mode.how_this_is_implemented: src/lib/storage.ts's isDemoMode() checks the env vars. A shared hook, src/lib/useAttemptController.ts, branches between the two implementations transparently so every page (StudyMode, PracticeQuiz, ExamSimulation) just calls begin()/select()/submit() without knowing which mode is active.
demo_mode_vs_real_mode.important_architectural_note: The full question bank JSON (including correct answers and all explanations) is bundled directly into the client-side JavaScript in BOTH modes. This means the 'sanitize questions before sending to browser' logic in the Netlify start-attempt function is only a partial security measure -- the browser's own JS bundle always has the answer key. Real security (an officer can't see another officer's SCORES/ATTEMPTS) is enforced by Supabase Row Level Security on the attempts tables, which is real and does work; but a technically sophisticated officer could find the correct answers in the JS bundle before answering. This has never been fully fixed -- documented as a known limitation.

question_schema.description: Every question in the bank (src/data/questions.json) follows this exact TypeScript interface (src/lib/types.ts, `Question`). This is the single most important schema for any AI generating new question content.

fields.id: string -- stable unique id, e.g. 'REG-0007' or 'MPD107-284'. Any unique string works; no fixed prefix convention is enforced by code.
fields.version: number -- starts at 1, incremented on each edit via the Question Editor
fields.status: 'draft' | 'published' | 'retired' -- only 'published' questions appear in any study/practice/exam mode
fields.topic: string, free text (often same as subtopic)
fields.subtopic: string, free text -- IMPORTANT: this field's wording is what the Map & Chart Reading classifier (src/lib/mapCategories.ts) pattern-matches against to sort visual questions into categories like 'Class B Airspace', 'METAR', etc. See map_chart_reading_system section for the exact keyword rules.
fields.acsCode: string, e.g. 'UA.II.A.K1' -- FAA Airman Certification Standards reference code
fields.conceptFamilyId: string -- groups near-duplicate question variants so the sampler avoids picking two very similar questions in the same attempt. Convention used so far: `${area}-${slugified subtopic}`
fields.choices: array of EXACTLY 3 objects: [{id: 'A'|'B'|'C', text: string, explanation: string}, ...] -- explanation is shown for that specific choice (why it's right or wrong) whenever feedback is revealed
fields.correctChoiceId: 'A' | 'B' | 'C' -- must match one of the choices' id
fields.sourceUrls: string[] -- real, verifiable URLs (14 CFR, ACS PDF, FAA supplement, etc.)
fields.figure: optional object -- present ONLY if this is a visual/chart question backed by a real bundled image. See figures section for the exact shape and the list of figure IDs that actually exist.
fields.resourceIds: string[] -- ids into src/data/resources.json (currently just 2 resources exist, see resources section)
fields.teachingExplanation: optional string -- full explanation tying the answer to the rule/figure (added in a later content pass, not present on every question)
fields.howToSolve: optional string -- a repeatable method for solving this TYPE of question
fields.reviewPrompt: optional string -- a prompt asking the learner to restate the reasoning themselves

figure_field_shape.figureId: string -- MUST exactly match one of the figure IDs listed in the figures section below. If it doesn't match a real bundled asset, the question should be marked status:'draft' instead of 'published' (a test enforces this: questionBank.test.ts fails the build if a published question's figure looks unresolved).
figure_field_shape.title: string, human-readable, e.g. 'Figure 23. Sectional Chart Excerpt (Savannah, GA area)'
figure_field_shape.editionOrDate: string -- the source document's edition/date, for honesty about currency
figure_field_shape.sourceUrl: string -- where the figure came from
figure_field_shape.isHistoricalTrainingCopy: boolean -- should always be true for these figures; triggers an on-screen 'training material, not for real navigation' notice

current_bank_size.note: This distribution deliberately matches the FAA/PSI exam content-percentage blueprint (see exam_blueprint section) -- 48/20/5/2/25 percent.

attempt_schema.description: An Attempt (src/lib/types.ts, `Attempt`) represents one run through Study Mode, Practice Quiz, or Exam Simulation.

fields.officerId: string (uuid in real mode, 'demo-officer' in demo mode)
fields.questionIds: string[] -- the exact question ids in this attempt, fixed at start
fields.answers: Record<questionId, {questionId, choiceId: string|null, flagged: boolean, answeredAt: string|null}>
fields.deadline: ISO datetime | null -- only set for simulation mode (2-hour limit)
fields.score: optional {correct, total, percent, byArea: [{area, correct, total, percent}], passedOverall, passedEveryArea}

readiness_logic.rule: An officer is 'Recommended to Schedule' the real FAA exam once they have 2 qualifying Exam Simulation attempts within the last 30 days. A qualifying attempt scores >=85% overall AND >=75% in EVERY area (percentages are floored, never rounded up).
readiness_logic.configurable_via: READINESS_CONFIG constant in readiness.ts (overallPercentMin: 85, areaPercentMin: 75, recentWindowDays: 30)

exam_blueprint.description: The scored-content percentage weighting the Exam Simulation and blueprint-weighted quizzes are built around. This is the CURRENT FAA/PSI blueprint, effective 2025-09-29 -- it replaced an older, different ACS percentage-range table. Verify this hasn't changed again before relying on it long-term.
exam_blueprint.source: PSI's UAG Applicant Information Bulletin (PSI is the FAA's testing vendor) -- https://media.psiexams.com/faa/UAG_Information_Bulletin.pdf

real_exam_facts.note: This app's Exam Simulation only replicates the 60 SCORED questions -- it does not add 5 fake unscored questions, since they're indistinguishable from scored ones on the real exam anyway and would teach nothing.

sixty_question_fixed_mix.note: This is the closest whole-number representation of the 48/20/5/2/25 percentages at 60 questions. Defined in TWO places that must be kept in sync: src/lib/types.ts SIMULATION_DISTRIBUTION and netlify/functions/start-attempt.ts's own copy (duplicated because the Netlify function bundle can't easily share code with the Vite client build).

2026_test_change_note.text: Beginning October 26, 2026, the FAA/PSI UAG exam can include image-based questions using CURRENT chart images not found in the printed testing supplement (FAA-CT-8080-2H). The printed supplement itself is not being removed from test centers on a set date. This app deliberately keeps teaching from the printed supplement's figures because the chart-reading SKILL transfers, while avoiding a UI that encourages memorizing one specific image.
2026_test_change_note.verified: Confirmed via a real FAA-hosted PDF (August 2026 Airman Testing Community Advisory) which corrected an earlier-stated October 27 date to October 26.

map_chart_reading_system.description: A parallel, cross-cutting way of navigating the SAME question bank, specifically for the 130 questions that have a real FAA figure attached. Two systems layer on top of each other: (1) the 13 'Map Categories' (a flat classification used for quick practice), and (2) the 14-lesson teaching Course (structured ground-school lessons that map to one or more of the 13 categories, or to a plain non-visual area).

the_13_map_categories.how_classification_works: A question qualifies as a 'map question' only if it has a non-null `figure` field. Its category is then determined by keyword-matching its `subtopic` + `topic` text (lowercased) against a fixed ordered list of rules in classifyMapQuestion(). IMPORTANT for content generation: if you write a new visual question, its `subtopic` wording should include one of these trigger phrases so it lands in the right bucket: 'class b' / 'class c' / 'class d' / 'class e' for airspace classes; 'ctaf', 'frequency', 'airport symbol', 'traffic pattern' etc. for the airport-symbols bucket; 'latitude'/'longitude'/'coordinate' for lat/long; 'moa'/'restricted'/'military training route'/'special-use' for special-use airspace; 'obstacle'/'terrain'/'mef'/'msl'/'agl' for obstacles/terrain; 'authorization'/'shelf'/'ceiling'/'notam' for boundaries/authorization; 'metar'/'taf'/'load factor' for those three. Anything that matches nothing falls into 'General Chart Reading' by default -- check src/lib/mapCategories.ts's exact function if precise control over bucketing matters.
the_13_map_categories.this_is_duplicated_server_side: netlify/functions/start-attempt.ts has its own copy of the exact same classifyMapQuestion logic (for the same reason as the exam blueprint -- functions and client can't easily share code). Any change to the classification rules must be made in BOTH files.

the_14_lesson_course.content_file: src/data/mapChartsCourse.json -- a large static JSON file, NOT auto-generated from the question bank. It was written externally (by the project owner using another AI) and dropped in wholesale.
the_14_lesson_course.schema: See src/lib/courseTypes.ts for the exact TypeScript shape (CourseContent, CourseLesson, etc.)
lesson_list: 3. MSL, AGL, Terrain, Obstacles & MEF (id: elevation-obstacles)
4. Airport Symbols, Frequencies & Traffic Patterns (id: airport-data)
5. Controlled vs. Uncontrolled Airspace -- the 3D picture (id: airspace-big-picture)
10. Airspace Boundaries, Authorization, NOTAMs & TFRs (id: authorization-notams)
11. Special-Use Airspace, MOAs, Restricted Areas, MTRs (id: special-use-airspace)
each_lesson_contains: question_bank_categories (array -- one or more of the 13 map categories, or 'non-visual Weather'/'Loading & Performance' to also pull non-visual questions)
knowledge_check (4-question instructional quiz, not scored toward readiness)
the_14_lesson_course.important_content_generation_note: If generating MORE lessons or editing existing ones in this exact JSON format, keep question_bank_categories values as EXACT string matches to the 13 category names above (or the two special non-visual tags) -- the app matches them by exact/prefix string comparison, not fuzzy matching.

figures.description: 18 real, extracted images from the actual official FAA 'Airman Knowledge Testing Supplement for Sport Pilot, Recreational Pilot, Remote Pilot, and Private Pilot' (2018 edition, document FAA-CT-8080-2H), which explicitly covers the UAG/Part 107 test. These are genuine scans/crops from the real PDF, not AI-generated. 15 of the 18 are currently referenced by at least one published question.
figures.storage_convention: Currently duplicated in two places: assets/figures/*.jpg (a 'canonical source' copy) and src/assets/figures/*.jpg (the copy Vite actually imports/bundles, via src/lib/figures.ts). THIS DUPLICATION IS NOT TECHNICALLY NECESSARY and should be simplified to just src/assets/figures/ next time this is touched -- noted so re-uploading isn't required twice going forward.
figures.how_a_question_gets_a_figure: The figure.figureId in a question's JSON must exactly match a key in the FIGURE_MAP object in src/lib/figures.ts, which maps that string id to the actual imported image file.

figures.rule: Never invent a new figureId for a question unless the matching image file has actually been added to both figure folders AND registered in src/lib/figures.ts's import list and FIGURE_MAP. A test (questionBank.test.ts) will fail the build otherwise if the question is marked published.

resources_library.note: Deliberately kept to just these 2 primary sources per the owner's explicit request -- no video resources are listed anywhere in this table (the lesson course's recommended_videos are separate, lesson-specific, and not in this table).

routes./login: Email + shared password sign-in (see auth section)
routes./: Home -- readiness status, average/highest score, per-area weak-spot breakdown, a congratulatory banner when 'Recommended to Schedule'
routes./study: Study Mode landing -- pick an FAA area (unrestricted practice, immediate feedback) or go to Map & Chart Reading
routes./study/map-charts: Map & Chart Reading landing -- 3 tabs: Study (14 lessons), Practice (13 category buttons), Mastery Check (mixed random pull from all visual questions)
routes./practice: Practice Quiz -- choose length (10/20/30/40/50/custom) and a single area or blueprint-weighted mixed. Immediate feedback per question. Does not count toward readiness.
routes./simulation: Exam Simulation -- exactly 60 questions in the fixed blueprint mix, 2-hour timer (persists across refresh), no feedback until submission, counts toward readiness
routes./results/:attemptId: Full question-by-question review for any past attempt (any mode), including teaching content, per-choice explanations, and a 'Report a problem with this question' button
routes./history: Every past attempt, any mode, with a delete (x) button per row
routes./coordinator: Coordinator-only dashboard -- officer roster, readiness/last-active/weakest-area at a glance, click a row to expand full area breakdown + recent attempts, program-wide weak topics, CSV export, question-bank status table
routes./coordinator/questions: Coordinator-only Question Editor -- search/filter all questions, full edit form (text, 3 choices + explanations, teaching fields, area/status/difficulty/ACS code), saves a version-history snapshot before each edit, plus a panel of open 'report a problem' submissions

practice_quiz_lengths: custom (any number, capped at bank size)
app_modes_and_pages.study_mode_behavior: Unlimited questions shown one at a time, immediate feedback + full explanation + teaching content after each answer, no fixed count, no score tracked toward readiness
app_modes_and_pages.exam_simulation_behavior: Submit button is disabled until every question is answered (except the timer running out, which force-submits regardless -- unanswered count as incorrect, matching the real exam's behavior)

auth_system.method: Email + password via Supabase Auth -- NOT magic link/OTP (that was tried first and abandoned due to email rate-limit and UX friction)
auth_system.current_setup: Every officer currently shares ONE department-wide password (chosen by the owner) rather than individual passwords -- a deliberate simplicity tradeoff the owner chose after being warned about the tradeoff (anyone who knows the password can sign in as any officer's email with no proof of identity). A brand-new email+correct-shared-password combination auto-creates that officer's account on first login (email confirmation is turned OFF in Supabase for this reason).
auth_system.roles: 'officer' (default) and 'coordinator' -- promotion to coordinator can only be done by someone with direct SQL access to Supabase (update part107_officers set role='coordinator' where email=...), there is no in-app way to self-promote or be promoted by another coordinator
auth_system.access_control: Enforced at 3 layers: (1) the coordinator nav link is hidden from non-coordinators, (2) each coordinator page independently checks the signed-in role and shows a plain refusal message otherwise, (3) Supabase RLS policies restrict what a non-coordinator's database queries can actually return, regardless of what the UI shows

database.shared_project_note: This app's tables live in the SAME Supabase project as the owner's other personal apps (Operation 200 weight tracker, Bill Planner). Every table is prefixed part107_ specifically to avoid any collision.

tables.part107_allowed_email_domains: domain allow-list (currently defined but not actually enforced anywhere in the sign-in code -- a known gap)
tables.part107_questions: mirrors the full Question schema above, snake_case columns (acs_code, correct_choice_id, teaching_explanation, how_to_solve, memory_tip, review_prompt, etc.)
tables.part107_question_versions: immutable snapshot of a question row taken every time the Question Editor saves a change, so historical attempt reports keep showing the wording an officer actually saw
tables.part107_question_problem_reports: officer-submitted 'something's wrong with this question' reports, status open/reviewed/dismissed
tables.part107_attempts: mirrors the Attempt schema above, snake_case (officer_id, question_ids, area_filter, started_at, deadline, submitted_at, finalized, score jsonb, timer_tampered)
tables.part107_attempt_answers: one row per question per attempt (attempt_id, question_id, choice_id, flagged, answered_at)
tables.part107_email_queue: queued officer/coordinator report emails, status pending/sent/failed, processed by a scheduled Netlify function -- NOT yet fully tested against a live Resend account
tables.part107_lesson_progress: officer_id + lesson_id -> completed_at, best_score (0-1) for the 14-lesson course

database.security_model: Row Level Security everywhere. The browser's anon key can only ever read its own officer's rows (or, for coordinators, everyone's rows) directly via Supabase's JS client for READS. All WRITES to attempts/scores go exclusively through Netlify Functions using a service-role key that bypasses RLS -- this is what makes 'a browser can't fake its own score' actually true at the database level, not just in the UI.

netlify_functions.start-attempt.ts: Creates a new attempt: selects question_ids server-side per the requested mode/area/skill-category/blueprint-weighting, computes the exam deadline server-side (not client clock), returns a 'sanitized' question payload (see the architectural caveat above about why this sanitization is only partially effective)
netlify_functions.submit-answer.ts: Records one answer to an in-progress attempt, validating the question/choice actually belongs to that attempt and that the attempt hasn't already been finalized or expired
netlify_functions.finalize-attempt.ts: Scores an attempt server-side (never trusts a browser-submitted score), idempotent (finalizing twice just returns the existing result), flags an attempt as timer_tampered if submitted past its deadline, queues report emails
netlify_functions.resend-report.ts: Lets an officer re-request their own report email, rate-limited (rate limiting itself is a documented no-op currently -- see known_limitations)
netlify_functions.send-queued-emails.ts: Scheduled function (every 2 minutes via netlify.toml) that drains the email queue via Resend -- refuses to send outside EMAIL_SANDBOX_DOMAIN while that env var is set, as a safety guard during development

design_system.palette: Navy (#0B2545 primary, #071A33 header), white, gold (#B8862E, reserved for readiness states and primary calls-to-action only), slate grays for text, mist (#F3F5F8) page background
design_system.typography: 'Source Serif 4' for headings, 'Inter' for UI/body text
design_system.aesthetic_intent: Reads as a professional training/operations console, not a marketing site or a generic SaaS dashboard -- gold is spent sparingly and specifically so it retains meaning

known_limitations_as_of_this_document: The full question bank (with correct answers) ships in the client JS bundle regardless of mode -- true answer-hiding before submission is not fully achieved architecturally, only enforced by UI convention
Rate limiting (checkRateLimit in netlify/functions/_shared.ts) is an intentional no-op, not yet implemented for real
Resend/email has never been tested against a live account -- RESEND_API_KEY etc. are likely still unconfigured
part107_allowed_email_domains exists in the schema but nothing in the sign-in code actually checks it
~1,200 individual per-choice explanations (400 questions x 3 choices) have not been independently re-verified against the regulations by a human other than the AI that wrote them
No automated accessibility audit has been run (built with keyboard nav/focus states/aria-live by design, but not tooling-verified)
The figures/ vs src/assets/figures/ duplication described above is unnecessary and should be simplified

The exam blueprint and Map & Chart classifier logic are each duplicated between the Vite client code and the Netlify Functions code (no shared package between them) -- a change to either must be made in both places or they'll silently disagree

how_to_make_common_changes.add_or_edit_questions_via_ui: Coordinator Dashboard -> Question Editor (only works with a live Supabase connection, not demo mode)
how_to_make_common_changes.add_or_edit_questions_in_bulk: Edit src/data/questions.json directly (must match the question_schema exactly), then re-run supabase/seed/import.mjs (or generate a SQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT file) to push it into the live database -- editing the JSON file alone only changes local demo-mode behavior until it's deployed and seeded
how_to_make_common_changes.add_a_new_figure: 1) Obtain the image (must be a real FAA source, never AI-generated). 2) Save it to src/assets/figures/ (see the duplication note above -- also add to assets/figures/ for now until that's simplified). 3) Add an import + FIGURE_MAP entry in src/lib/figures.ts. 4) Reference its figureId from a question's figure field, set that question's status to 'published' only once steps 1-3 are done.
how_to_make_common_changes.add_a_new_lesson: Add an entry to the lessons array in src/data/mapChartsCourse.json matching the CourseLesson shape in src/lib/courseTypes.ts. No code change needed -- the landing/lesson pages read this file dynamically.
how_to_make_common_changes.change_the_exam_blueprint: Update SIMULATION_DISTRIBUTION and FAA_PUBLISHED_RANGE in src/lib/types.ts, AND the duplicate SIMULATION_DISTRIBUTION constant in netlify/functions/start-attempt.ts -- both must match or client/server will disagree.
how_to_make_common_changes.deploy_a_change: This project is deployed via GitHub -> Netlify (not the single-file drag-and-drop method anymore). Push changed files to the GitHub repo (the owner currently does this by editing/uploading files directly through GitHub's web UI, not git CLI, since dev work happens on a work computer without Node.js installed and without terminal access), and Netlify auto-builds and deploys on push to main.
